label: Card Financial Condition
title: Card Financial Condition
summary: Use a Card Financial Condition to show one coverage score with a short reading, a hint on what's missing, and one button.
corePrinciple: One score, one gap, one next step.

anatomy.title: A score, a hint, and a button
anatomy.description: A white card puts a title and one line beside a 60 px score ring. Under them sit an inline nudge with up to two lines, a divider, and one button.
blocks: The topic in 16 px bold; it wraps rather than cutting off.
One short line on what the score covers.
A 60 px Circular Progress Bar: empty while Inactive, value out of 100 when Active.
An inline Nudge with nudgeBody; a line break starts its second line.
A 1 px rule; showDivider removes it.
A purple Button with buttonLabel; onPressButton runs your action.

configuration.title: Brand, status, and sections
configuration.description: AppearanceBrand colours the ring and the nudge: the card defaults to Neutral, and the button stays purple. For a score that’s good or bad, set Semantic Intent to System and pick AppearanceSystem: the ring, the nudge, and the button take the status colour. Emphasis Medium or Low makes the ring and the button paler. showNudge, showDivider, and showButton remove their parts; progressSlot, nudgeSlot, and buttonSlot replace them with your own components.

states.title: Inactive or Active
states.description: progressState decides whether the ring shows a score. Inactive, the default, draws an empty ring with a dash; Active fills value out of 100 and prints the number, or valueLabel in its place. The card has no pressed or disabled state: only the button acts.

sizing.title: Your screen sets the width
sizing.description: The card has no width of its own: it fills its host, and Figma draws it at 343 px. It’s as tall as its content, with 16 px padding, 8 px between parts, and 16 px between the text and the 60 px ring. The button is always Figma’s 32 px, with 14 px text, whatever Context the card has.

content.title: Name it, read it, act on it
content.description: Use a one- or two-word title for the topic and one short line for the body. Keep the nudge to two lines with a line break between them, and label the button with a verb. The default spoken name reads the title, the score, and the body, such as “Protection, 72 out of 100. Check your coverage and gaps”. While the ring is Inactive, it leaves out the score: “Protection. Check your coverage and gaps”.

sources.title: Use the public Card Financial Condition contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78, built from Biscuit’s main at dbe0e02 (27 October) and taken from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Card/FinancialCondition is one 343 × 181 component with no properties and an Inactive ring; its nudge is the retired Nudge with a purple sparkle, which no mode reproduces, so this page follows the package’s Neutral default. The button is Figma’s 32 px at any Context. The card stays white in every mode, and its default spoken name includes the score only while the ring is Active. The published Storybook still shows the older generated page.
